newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Lone Star up after JCI reveals stake.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Lone Star up after JCI reveals stake.

text.p: The shares of Lone Star Exploration NL rose sharply on light volume on Friday after South African mining house JCI Ltd revealed that it had acquired an 8.51 percent direct stake in the miner.
At 11.20 a.m. (0020 GMT), Lone Star shares were seven cents higher at A$0.71 on turnover of 70,000 shares.
In a statement to the Australian Stock Exchange, Lone Star said JCI had bought 7.71 million shares at prices ranging between A$1.15 to A$1.40 per share.
Last month Lone Star bought out its partners, including JCI, in the Awak Mas gold project in Indonesia for about A$50.6 million.

Under the deal Lone Star agreed to purchase JCI's free-carried 10 percent stake for a consideration of 25 million shares in Lone Star. As a part of the deal, JCI agreed to assist Lone Star by sourcing US$20 million of non-recourse funding for the Awak Mas mine development, on Sulawesi island.

"JCI Ltd were prepared to pay up to A$1.40 for 4.65 million shares which suggests JCI have a positive view on the real value of Lone Star's Awak Mas Resource and its potential to expand in the near term," said Lone Star chairman, Bob Wilde.

The other partner in Awak Mas was Gascoyne Gold Mines NL which held a 45 percent stake. Lone Star has agreed to pay Gascoyne US$15 million on settlement, US$20 million over three years and to issue Gascoyne 10 million ordinary Lone Star shares.
